title: Optimization I
subject: Mathematics

cards.prompt: Define Coercivity existence route. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The growth of an objective toward positive infinity as the variable norm diverges which can confine relevant sublevel sets.
required_concepts: The growth of an objective toward positive infinity as the variable norm diverges which can confine relevant sublevel sets.
major_error_concepts: Calling any positive objective coercive.

cards.prompt: Define Constraint and feasible set. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A condition restricting admissible variables and the set satisfying every domain and constraint condition.
required_concepts: A condition restricting admissible variables and the set satisfying every domain and constraint condition.
major_error_concepts: Checking each constraint separately but accepting a point that does not satisfy their intersection.

cards.prompt: Define Decision variable. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A quantity selected by the optimizer rather than observed or fixed by the modeler.
required_concepts: A quantity selected by the optimizer rather than observed or fixed by the modeler.
major_error_concepts: Optimizing over a because both letters appear in the objective.

cards.prompt: Define Existence by compactness and continuity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The sufficient condition that a continuous objective attains a minimum on a nonempty compact feasible set.
required_concepts: The sufficient condition that a continuous objective attains a minimum on a nonempty compact feasible set.
major_error_concepts: Claiming compactness is necessary for every optimization problem with a solution.

cards.prompt: Define Feasible point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A domain-admissible point satisfying every constraint independent of its objective quality.
required_concepts: A domain-admissible point satisfying every constraint independent of its objective quality.
major_error_concepts: Calling a point infeasible merely because it is suboptimal.

cards.prompt: Define First-order necessary condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The zero-gradient condition at an unconstrained differentiable interior local minimizer.
required_concepts: The zero-gradient condition at an unconstrained differentiable interior local minimizer.
major_error_concepts: Applying the condition at a nondifferentiable point or boundary without qualification.

cards.prompt: Define Global minimizer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A feasible point whose objective is no larger than at every feasible point.
required_concepts: A feasible point whose objective is no larger than at every feasible point.
major_error_concepts: Proving only that nearby points are worse and claiming globality without structure.

cards.prompt: Define Infeasible problem. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An optimization model whose feasible set is empty and therefore has no feasible optimizer.
required_concepts: An optimization model whose feasible set is empty and therefore has no feasible optimizer.
major_error_concepts: Calling the objective unbounded without first checking feasibility.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Infimum versus minimum.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The greatest lower bound of attainable objective values distinguished from a value attained at a feasible optimizer.
required_concepts: The infimum is the greatest lower bound of the attainable objective values and need not itself be attained.
A minimum is an objective value attained by at least one feasible optimizer.
Attainment is the decisive distinction: every minimum value is the infimum, but an infimum need not be a minimum.
major_error_concepts: Writing minimum 0 at x=0 even though x=0 is excluded.

cards.prompt: Define Local minimizer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A feasible point no worse than all feasible points in some neighborhood of that point.
required_concepts: A feasible point no worse than all feasible points in some neighborhood of that point.
major_error_concepts: Calling every local minimizer globally optimal.

cards.prompt: Define Optimization-problem parameter. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A fixed input indexing a family of optimization problems whose perturbation may change the solution or value.
required_concepts: A fixed input indexing a family of optimization problems whose perturbation may change the solution or value.
major_error_concepts: Substituting one numerical a and forgetting the model is parameterized.

cards.prompt: Define Objective sense and value. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared minimization or maximization direction and scalar objective value distinguished from the optimizer itself.
required_concepts: The declared minimization or maximization direction and scalar objective value distinguished from the optimizer itself.
major_error_concepts: Calling x=3 the minimum value or omitting the objective sense.

cards.prompt: Define Second-order necessary condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The positive-semidefinite Hessian condition at a twice-differentiable unconstrained interior local minimizer.
required_concepts: The positive-semidefinite Hessian condition at a twice-differentiable unconstrained interior local minimizer.
major_error_concepts: Calling a PSD Hessian sufficient for a strict local minimum in all cases.

cards.prompt: Define Second-order sufficient condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The positive-definite Hessian at a stationary point condition ensuring a strict local minimum.
required_concepts: The positive-definite Hessian at a stationary point condition ensuring a strict local minimum.
major_error_concepts: Using positive definiteness without first checking stationarity.

cards.prompt: Define Stationary point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An interior differentiable point with zero gradient which is a candidate rather than an automatic minimum.
required_concepts: An interior differentiable point with zero gradient which is a candidate rather than an automatic minimum.
major_error_concepts: Equating zero gradient with optimality.

cards.prompt: Define Strict and isolated local minimizer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A local minimizer with strict inequality for nearby distinct feasible points distinguished from the topological property of being the only local minimizer nearby.
required_concepts: A strict local minimizer has strictly smaller objective value than nearby distinct feasible points.
Strict local minimality is distinct from being the only local minimizer in a neighborhood.
major_error_concepts: Treating strict local minimality and global uniqueness as identical claims.

cards.prompt: Define Unbounded-below problem. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A feasible minimization problem with objective values decreasing without a finite lower bound.
required_concepts: A feasible minimization problem with objective values decreasing without a finite lower bound.
major_error_concepts: Calling it infeasible because no finite minimizer exists.

cards.prompt: Define Unique minimizer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The sole feasible point attaining the optimal value rather than merely a point returned by one solver run.
required_concepts: The sole feasible point attaining the optimal value rather than merely a point returned by one solver run.
major_error_concepts: Calling the solver's selected point unique because only one point was displayed.

cards.prompt: Define Affine image and preimage convexity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The preservation of convexity by affine images and by inverse images under affine maps.
required_concepts: The preservation of convexity by affine images and by inverse images under affine maps.
major_error_concepts: Claiming an arbitrary nonlinear preimage preserves convexity.

cards.prompt: Define Affine set. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A set containing every affine combination of any two of its points for unrestricted real coefficients summing to one.
required_concepts: A set containing every affine combination of any two of its points for unrestricted real coefficients summing to one.
major_error_concepts: Calling a bounded line segment affine because it is convex.

cards.prompt: Define Concave function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A function whose negative is convex or whose graph lies above its chords.
required_concepts: A function whose negative is convex or whose graph lies above its chords.
major_error_concepts: Calling log x concave on all real numbers despite its domain.

cards.prompt: Define Convex combination. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A weighted sum theta x plus (1-theta)y with theta in [0,1] that lies on the segment between x and y.
required_concepts: A weighted sum theta x plus (1-theta)y with theta in [0,1] that lies on the segment between x and y.
major_error_concepts: Using weights that do not sum to one and calling the result a convex combination.

cards.prompt: Define Convex cone. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A set closed under nonnegative linear combinations and containing scaled rays from the origin.
required_concepts: A set closed under nonnegative linear combinations and containing scaled rays from the origin.
major_error_concepts: Calling an offset halfspace a cone although it is not closed under positive scaling from the origin.

cards.prompt: Define Convex function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A function whose value at every convex combination is no greater than the same convex combination of endpoint values on a convex domain.
required_concepts: A function whose value at every convex combination is no greater than the same convex combination of endpoint values on a convex domain.
major_error_concepts: Checking convexity without specifying a convex domain.

cards.prompt: Define convex optimization problem.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The combination of convex feasible set convex objective for minimization or concave objective for maximization and compatible constraint forms.
required_concepts: The combination of convex feasible set convex objective for minimization or concave objective for maximization and compatible constraint forms.
major_error_concepts: Calling maximization of a convex function a convex optimization problem.

cards.prompt: Define Convex set. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A set containing the complete line segment between every pair of its points.
required_concepts: A set containing the complete line segment between every pair of its points.
major_error_concepts: Checking only one pair of points and declaring an arbitrary set convex.

cards.prompt: Define Convex sublevel set. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The set {x:f(x)<=alpha} which is convex for every alpha when f is convex.
required_concepts: The set {x:f(x)<=alpha} which is convex for every alpha when f is convex.
major_error_concepts: Claiming convex sublevel sets for all alpha are sufficient for ordinary convexity rather than quasiconvexity.

cards.prompt: Define Convexity under intersection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The closure property that any intersection of convex sets is convex.
required_concepts: The closure property that any intersection of convex sets is convex.
major_error_concepts: Claiming a union of convex sets is always convex.

cards.prompt: Define Epigraph criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The equivalence that a function is convex exactly when its epigraph {(x,t): f(x)<=t} is convex.
required_concepts: The equivalence that a function is convex exactly when its epigraph {(x,t): f(x)<=t} is convex.
major_error_concepts: Using a subgraph rather than epigraph for convexity.

cards.prompt: Define Euclidean ball and norm ball. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A set {x: norm(x-c)<=r} that is convex for any norm and positive radius.
required_concepts: A set {x: norm(x-c)<=r} that is convex for any norm and positive radius.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every visually round set is a norm ball.

cards.prompt: Define First-order convexity condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The global supporting-hyperplane inequality f(y)>=f(x)+gradient f(x) transpose (y-x) for differentiable convex f on a convex open domain.
required_concepts: The global supporting-hyperplane inequality f(y)>=f(x)+gradient f(x) transpose (y-x) for differentiable convex f on a convex open domain.
major_error_concepts: Using the inequality as a local approximation only and ignoring its global consequence under convexity.

cards.prompt: Define Hyperplane and halfspace. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: For a nonzero vector a in R^n, the affine hyperplane {x:a^T x=b} has codimension one and normal a. Its two closed halfspaces are {x:a^T x≤b} and {x:a^T x≥b}; strict inequalities give their open sides. With a=0 the equality is either all of R^n or empty, so it does not define a hyperplane.
required_concepts: The normal a is nonzero.
The equality defines the hyperplane and the inequality sides define halfspaces.
a is a normal direction, not in general a point on the hyperplane.
major_error_concepts: The equation 0^T x=0 defines a codimension-one hyperplane in R^n.

cards.term: Jensen inequality for convex-objective bounds: role
cards.prompt: What is Jensen inequality for convex-objective bounds used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It moves a convex objective through averaging and underlies convexity, mixture, and expectation bounds in optimization; the direction reverses for concave functions and equality needs additional structure.
required_concepts: It moves a convex objective through averaging and underlies convexity, mixture, and expectation bounds in optimization
the direction reverses for concave functions and equality needs additional structure.
major_error_concepts: Reversing Jensen's direction for a convex function.

cards.prompt: State Jensen inequality for convex-objective bounds, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** For convex f on convex C, x_i in C, lambda_i>=0, and sum_i lambda_i=1, f(sum_i lambda_i x_i)<=sum_i lambda_i f(x_i). Probabilistically, if X is integrable, X lies in C almost surely, E[X] lies in C, f is convex on C, and f(X) is integrable for the finite-valued expectation form, then f(E[X])<=E[f(X)].
required_concepts: The finite form uses x_i in convex C, nonnegative weights, and weights summing to one.
f(sum_i lambda_i x_i)<=sum_i lambda_i f(x_i).
For the probabilistic form, X is integrable, X lies in C almost surely, and E[X] lies in the convex domain C.
f is convex on C and f(X) is integrable for the finite-valued expectation form.
The probabilistic conclusion is f(E[X])<=E[f(X)].
major_error_concepts: Reversing Jensen's direction for a convex function.

cards.prompt: Define Lipschitz gradient and smoothness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The bound norm(gradient f(x)-gradient f(y))<=L norm(x-y) yielding a quadratic upper model.
required_concepts: The bound norm(gradient f(x)-gradient f(y))<=L norm(x-y) yielding a quadratic upper model.
major_error_concepts: Calling a bounded function Lipschitz-smooth without bounding its gradient change.

cards.prompt: Define Relative interior. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The interior taken within a set's affine hull rather than the full ambient space.
required_concepts: The interior taken within a set's affine hull rather than the full ambient space.
major_error_concepts: Calling every lower-dimensional convex set interiorless for all convex-analysis purposes.

cards.prompt: Define Second-order convexity condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The positive-semidefinite Hessian criterion for twice-differentiable convexity on an open convex domain.
required_concepts: The positive-semidefinite Hessian criterion for twice-differentiable convexity on an open convex domain.
major_error_concepts: Checking only positive diagonal Hessian entries.

cards.prompt: Define Strict convexity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The strict chord inequality for distinct points and interior weights which implies at most one minimizer on a convex feasible set.
required_concepts: The strict chord inequality for distinct points and interior weights which implies at most one minimizer on a convex feasible set.
major_error_concepts: Claiming failure of strong convexity means failure of strict convexity.

cards.prompt: State differentiable mu-strong convexity using the Euclidean quadratic-support convention, and distinguish uniqueness from existence.
cards.definition: A differentiable function f on an open convex domain is mu-strongly convex, in the Euclidean convention with mu>0, if f(y)≥f(x)+grad f(x)^T(y-x)+(mu/2)||y-x||² for all x,y in the domain. Equivalently f(x)-(mu/2)||x||² is convex. This implies at most one minimizer on a convex feasible set, but does not by itself guarantee attainment on an arbitrary open domain.
required_concepts: Use a fixed positive modulus mu and the factor mu/2.
The lower quadratic-support bound holds for all domain points.
Strong convexity implies uniqueness if a minimum exists, not unconditional attainment.
major_error_concepts: Strong convexity means f(y)≥f(x)+grad f(x)^T(y-x) with no fixed positive quadratic term, and always guarantees attainment on any open domain.

cards.prompt: Define Active constraint. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An inequality holding at equality at a specified feasible point.
required_concepts: An inequality holding at equality at a specified feasible point.
major_error_concepts: Calling every model constraint active at an optimum.

cards.prompt: Define Basic feasible solution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A standard-form feasible solution associated with a basis whose nonbasic variables are zero, allowing degeneracy.
required_concepts: A standard-form feasible solution associated with a basis whose nonbasic variables are zero, allowing degeneracy.
major_error_concepts: Calling any feasible interior point a BFS.

cards.prompt: Define Canonical problem certificate matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The reconciliation of model class feasibility geometry optimizer value and independent certificate for LP least-squares and QP examples.
required_concepts: The reconciliation of model class feasibility geometry optimizer value and independent certificate for LP least-squares and QP examples.
major_error_concepts: Using the same residual meaning for unrelated problem classes.

cards.prompt: Define Extreme point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A feasible point not expressible as a nontrivial convex combination of two distinct feasible points.
required_concepts: A feasible point not expressible as a nontrivial convex combination of two distinct feasible points.
major_error_concepts: Calling every boundary point an extreme point.

cards.prompt: What is Farkas alternative used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It converts infeasibility of a nonnegative linear system into an explicit separating certificate under one frozen sign convention.
required_concepts: It supplies an infeasibility certificate for Ax=b, x>=0.
The certificate signs depend on the frozen theorem form.
major_error_concepts: Mixing certificates from incompatible Farkas sign conventions.

cards.prompt: State Farkas' alternative in the Ax=b, x>=0 sign convention, including both exclusive systems.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** Exactly one of the following holds: (i) there exists x>=0 with Ax=b; or (ii) there exists y with A^T y>=0 and b^T y<0.
required_concepts: The primal system is Ax=b with x>=0.
The certificate system is A^T y>=0 with b^T y<0.
Exactly one of the two systems is feasible.
major_error_concepts: Mixing signs from different Farkas variants.

cards.prompt: What claim does Indefinite quadratic counterexample refute, and why?
cards.definition: **Definition.** The quadratic q(x,y)=x^2-y^2 refutes the claim that every quadratic objective is convex. Its Hessian is diag(2,-2), so the x direction has positive curvature while the y direction has negative curvature; the Hessian is indefinite and q is not convex.
required_concepts: The false claim is that every quadratic objective is convex.
A concrete witness is q(x,y)=x^2-y^2.
The Hessian of q is diag(2,-2), with positive curvature in the x direction and negative curvature in the y direction.
Because the Hessian is indefinite rather than positive semidefinite, q is not convex.
major_error_concepts: Checking only the positive x curvature and calling it convex.

cards.prompt: Define Least-squares problem. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The minimization of squared residual norm norm(Ax-b) squared with normal equations and projection geometry.
required_concepts: The minimization of squared residual norm norm(Ax-b) squared with normal equations and projection geometry.
major_error_concepts: Averaging coefficients without deriving the residual objective.

cards.prompt: Define Least-squares projection certificate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The orthogonality A transpose(b-Ax star)=0 showing the fitted vector is the orthogonal projection onto the column space.
required_concepts: The orthogonality A transpose(b-Ax star)=0 showing the fitted vector is the orthogonal projection onto the column space.
major_error_concepts: Checking only a small residual norm rather than orthogonality and optimality.

cards.prompt: Define Linear program. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An optimization problem with a linear objective and affine equality and inequality constraints.
required_concepts: An optimization problem with a linear objective and affine equality and inequality constraints.
major_error_concepts: Treating a product xy as linear because each variable appears to the first power.

cards.prompt: Define LP complementary slackness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The zero products linking each primal slack with its dual variable and each dual slack with its primal variable at an optimal primal-dual pair.
required_concepts: The zero products linking each primal slack with its dual variable and each dual slack with its primal variable at an optimal primal-dual pair.
major_error_concepts: Claiming a binding constraint must have a strictly positive multiplier.

cards.prompt: Define LP degeneracy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A basic feasible solution with at least one basic variable equal to zero which can correspond to multiple bases and stalled pivots.
required_concepts: A basic feasible solution with at least one basic variable equal to zero which can correspond to multiple bases and stalled pivots.
major_error_concepts: Equating degeneracy with infeasibility or multiple optimal solutions.

cards.prompt: Construct the dual of min c^T x subject to Ax=b and x≥0, stating every dual sign and inequality convention.
cards.definition: For the primal LP minimize c^T x subject to Ax=b and x≥0, the dual is maximize b^T y subject to A^T y≤c, with y unrestricted in sign. For feasible x,y, b^T y≤c^T x. Changing primal inequality directions, variable signs, or optimization sense changes the dual convention and must be derived consistently.
required_concepts: Freeze the primal as min c^T x, Ax=b, x≥0.
The dual is max b^T y, A^T y≤c, with y free.
Compatible feasible objectives satisfy b^T y≤c^T x.
major_error_concepts: For min c^T x with Ax=b,x≥0, the dual always requires y≥0 and A^T y≥c.

cards.term: LP optimal face and alternate optima
cards.prompt: Define LP optimal face and alternate optima. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The face on which the linear objective is constant at its optimum, possibly containing multiple extreme points.
required_concepts: The face on which the linear objective is constant at its optimum, possibly containing multiple extreme points.
major_error_concepts: Reporting the first returned vertex as a unique optimum.

cards.prompt: State an LP standard-form convention and explain slack, surplus, and free-variable transformations.
cards.definition: One standard LP convention is minimize c^T x subject to Ax=b and x≥0. A ≤ inequality becomes an equality by adding a nonnegative slack; a ≥ inequality uses a nonnegative surplus subtracted from the left side. An unrestricted scalar z can be represented as z=z_plus-z_minus with both components nonnegative. These transformations preserve feasible solutions and objective values through the reconstruction map, but split-variable representations need not be unique.
required_concepts: Declare the chosen standard form.
Use the correct slack or surplus sign.
Free-variable splitting preserves the reconstructed variable but is not one-to-one.
major_error_concepts: Every real value z has exactly one representation z=z_plus-z_minus with z_plus,z_minus≥0.

cards.prompt: Define LP unbounded ray certificate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A feasible direction d preserving feasibility along x+td for all t>=0 and strictly improving the objective without bound.
required_concepts: A feasible direction d preserving feasibility along x+td for all t>=0 and strictly improving the objective without bound.
major_error_concepts: Using a direction that eventually violates a constraint.

cards.prompt: Define LP weak duality. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The bound that every dual-feasible objective is no greater than every primal-feasible objective for a minimization primal.
required_concepts: The bound that every dual-feasible objective is no greater than every primal-feasible objective for a minimization primal.
major_error_concepts: Claiming either feasible point is optimal merely from weak duality.

cards.prompt: Define Normal equations as least-squares optimality. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The stationarity system A transpose A x=A transpose b for ordinary least squares, with uniqueness requiring full column rank.
required_concepts: The stationarity system A transpose A x=A transpose b for ordinary least squares, with uniqueness requiring full column rank.
major_error_concepts: Claiming A transpose A is invertible for every A.

cards.prompt: Define Polyhedron. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An intersection of finitely many affine halfspaces and hyperplanes that forms an LP feasible region.
required_concepts: An intersection of finitely many affine halfspaces and hyperplanes that forms an LP feasible region.
major_error_concepts: Calling every convex set polyhedral.

cards.prompt: Define PSD quadratic objective. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The condition that the symmetric quadratic matrix is positive semidefinite so its Hessian supplies convexity.
required_concepts: The condition that the symmetric quadratic matrix is positive semidefinite so its Hessian supplies convexity.
major_error_concepts: Requiring positive definiteness for convexity.

cards.prompt: Define Quadratic program. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An optimization problem with a quadratic objective one-half x transpose Qx plus q transpose x plus r and affine constraints.
required_concepts: An optimization problem with a quadratic objective one-half x transpose Qx plus q transpose x plus r and affine constraints.
major_error_concepts: Calling every QP convex.

cards.prompt: Define Armijo sufficient decrease. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The inequality f(x+alpha p)<=f(x)+c1 alpha gradient f(x) transpose p with c1 in (0,1).
required_concepts: The inequality f(x+alpha p)<=f(x)+c1 alpha gradient f(x) transpose p with c1 in (0,1).
major_error_concepts: Reversing the inequality or using a non-descent direction without qualification.

cards.prompt: Define Backtracking line search. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The geometric reduction of an initial trial step until a sufficient-decrease condition passes.
required_concepts: The geometric reduction of an initial trial step until a sufficient-decrease condition passes.
major_error_concepts: Accepting the first lower objective without checking the declared condition.

cards.prompt: Define Smooth strongly convex condition number. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The ratio L/mu for a smooth strongly convex objective or lambda_max/lambda_min for an SPD quadratic, predicting anisotropy and rate difficulty.
required_concepts: The ratio L/mu for a smooth strongly convex objective or lambda_max/lambda_min for an SPD quadratic, predicting anisotropy and rate difficulty.
major_error_concepts: Using a condition number when the smallest relevant eigenvalue is zero without stating singularity.

cards.prompt: State a concrete O(1/k) objective-gap bound for fixed-step gradient descent on a smooth convex function.
cards.definition: Let f:R^n→R be convex and differentiable with L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0, and let x* be a minimizer. Gradient descent x_(k+1)=x_k-grad f(x_k)/L satisfies f(x_k)-f(x*)≤L||x_0-x*||²/(2k) for k≥1. This is a worst-case objective-gap upper bound, not an exact per-iteration equality or a claim of O(1/k) distance error.
required_concepts: Assume convexity, L-smoothness, and an attained minimum.
Use the fixed step 1/L.
State objective gap ≤L||x_0-x*||²/(2k), k≥1.
major_error_concepts: For every convex function and every step size, the iterate distance is exactly 1/k after k updates.

cards.prompt: State weak and strong Wolfe curvature conditions and distinguish them from Armijo sufficient decrease.
cards.definition: For a descent direction p, a weak Wolfe curvature condition is grad f(x+alpha p)^T p≥c2 grad f(x)^T p. Together with Armijo use 0<c1<c2<1 and alpha>0. The strong Wolfe version instead requires |grad f(x+alpha p)^T p|≤c2 |grad f(x)^T p|. These conditions control the post-step directional derivative; Armijo alone controls objective decrease and is not a full Wolfe search.
required_concepts: State the weak Wolfe directional-derivative inequality.
Use compatible constants 0<c1<c2<1 with Armijo and a descent direction.
Distinguish strong Wolfe absolute-value control from Armijo alone.
major_error_concepts: Armijo sufficient decrease by itself is both the weak and strong Wolfe curvature condition.

cards.prompt: Define Descent direction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A direction p with gradient f(x) transpose p<0 at a nonstationary differentiable point, guaranteeing decrease only for sufficiently small positive steps.
required_concepts: A direction p with gradient f(x) transpose p<0 at a nonstationary differentiable point, guaranteeing decrease only for sufficiently small positive steps.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every positive step along a descent direction decreases the objective.

cards.prompt: What is Descent lemma used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It upper-bounds a smooth objective after a step by a linear term plus quadratic curvature control, yielding safe step sizes and gradient-descent decrease; it requires Lipschitz gradient control and does not imply convexity.
required_concepts: It upper-bounds a smooth objective after a step by a linear term plus quadratic curvature control, yielding safe step sizes and gradient-descent decrease
it requires Lipschitz gradient control and does not imply convexity.
major_error_concepts: Using the lemma without an L-Lipschitz gradient.

cards.prompt: State Descent lemma, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If f is differentiable on a convex domain containing [x,y] and grad f is L-Lipschitz there, then f(y)<=f(x)+grad f(x)^T(y-x)+(L/2)||y-x||^2.
required_concepts: f is differentiable on a convex domain containing the segment [x,y].
grad f is L-Lipschitz on that domain.
major_error_concepts: Using the lemma without an L-Lipschitz gradient.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Exact versus inexact line search.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between minimizing the one-dimensional ray objective and finding a step satisfying sufficient conditions.
required_concepts: Exact line search minimizes the one-dimensional objective along the chosen search ray.
Inexact line search accepts a step that satisfies declared sufficient-decrease or curvature conditions without requiring the ray minimum.
A step that merely decreases the objective can be inexact and does not thereby become the exact ray minimizer.
major_error_concepts: Calling a backtracking step exact because it decreased the objective.

cards.prompt: Define Gradient descent. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The first-order iteration x_{k+1}=x_k-alpha_k gradient f(x_k) under a specified step-size rule.
required_concepts: The first-order iteration x_{k+1}=x_k-alpha_k gradient f(x_k) under a specified step-size rule.
major_error_concepts: Using the gradient at x0 for every iteration.

cards.prompt: Define Ill-conditioned valley. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The geometry where level sets have widely different curvature scales and first-order iterates zigzag or progress slowly.
required_concepts: The geometry where level sets have widely different curvature scales and first-order iterates zigzag or progress slowly.
major_error_concepts: Calling poor scaling proof that the objective is nonconvex.

cards.prompt: Define Iterative optimization method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A state transition x_{k+1}=T_k(x_k) whose initialization direction step rule stopping test and evidence are part of the algorithm.
required_concepts: A state transition x_{k+1}=T_k(x_k) whose initialization direction step rule stopping test and evidence are part of the algorithm.
major_error_concepts: Giving only the update formula without the initialization or step rule.

cards.prompt: Define Preconditioned gradient step. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The update x_{k+1}=x_k-alpha P gradient f(x_k) with SPD P chosen to reshape local geometry.
required_concepts: The update x_{k+1}=x_k-alpha P gradient f(x_k) with SPD P chosen to reshape local geometry.
major_error_concepts: Using a nonsymmetric or indefinite P while claiming the standard metric interpretation.

cards.prompt: Define Quadratic spectral trajectory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The decomposition of gradient descent on a PSD quadratic into eigen-directions multiplied by 1-alpha lambda_i each step.
required_concepts: The decomposition of gradient descent on a PSD quadratic into eigen-directions multiplied by 1-alpha lambda_i each step.
major_error_concepts: Using one scalar rate while ignoring the spectrum.

cards.term: Safe fixed step for smooth convex descent
cards.prompt: State a safe positive fixed-step range for gradient descent and the resulting smoothness decrease bound.
cards.definition: For an L-smooth differentiable f with L>0, take x_next=x-alpha grad f(x) and 0<alpha≤1/L, with the step segment in the smoothness domain. Then f(x_next)≤f(x)-alpha(1-L alpha/2)||grad f(x)||²≤f(x)-(alpha/2)||grad f(x)||². This proves strict decrease at a nonstationary point. Convexity is not needed for this one-step decrease, though it matters for global rate conclusions.
required_concepts: Require a positive step 0<alpha≤1/L and L>0.
Smoothness yields the stated negative gradient-norm-squared bound.
Nonzero gradient gives strict decrease; this alone is not a global convergence theorem.
major_error_concepts: Any alpha≤1/L, including alpha=-1/L, guarantees descent.

cards.prompt: Define Search direction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The vector p_k defining a local ray x_k+alpha p_k before a step length is selected.
required_concepts: The vector p_k defining a local ray x_k+alpha p_k before a step length is selected.
major_error_concepts: Calling the direction itself the next iterate.

cards.prompt: Define Step length. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The nonnegative scalar alpha mapping a direction to an actual trial or accepted iterate.
required_concepts: The nonnegative scalar alpha mapping a direction to an actual trial or accepted iterate.
major_error_concepts: Changing the direction while describing only a changed step length.

cards.prompt: Define Stopping criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A declared test using gradient norm step norm objective change iteration budget or residuals whose meaning depends on scaling and problem class.
required_concepts: A declared test using gradient norm step norm objective change iteration budget or residuals whose meaning depends on scaling and problem class.
major_error_concepts: Stopping because printed digits no longer change.

cards.prompt: State a geometric objective-gap bound for gradient descent with step 1/L on a mu-strongly convex L-smooth function.
cards.definition: Let f:R^n→R have L-Lipschitz gradient and be mu-strongly convex, with 0<mu≤L. For x_(k+1)=x_k-grad f(x_k)/L and its unique minimizer x*, f(x_k)-f(x*)≤(1-mu/L)^k [f(x_0)-f(x*)]. Linear convergence means this geometric objective-gap bound, not a fixed additive improvement; alternative valid rate bounds must state their norm and step convention.
required_concepts: Assume L-smoothness and mu-strong convexity with positive constants.
Use step 1/L.
The objective gap contracts geometrically with a valid factor 1-mu/L.
major_error_concepts: Linear convergence means every iteration subtracts the same positive constant from the objective gap until it reaches zero.

cards.prompt: Define Variable scaling. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The invertible change of coordinates used to reduce anisotropy while preserving a mapped optimization problem.
required_concepts: The invertible change of coordinates used to reduce anisotropy while preserving a mapped optimization problem.
major_error_concepts: Changing coordinates but forgetting to transform constraints and the final solution back.

cards.prompt: Define Actual-to-predicted reduction ratio. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The quotient [f(x)-f(x+p)]/[m(0)-m(p)] used to judge a trust-region model and update its radius.
required_concepts: The quotient [f(x)-f(x+p)]/[m(0)-m(p)] used to judge a trust-region model and update its radius.
major_error_concepts: Dividing predicted by actual reduction or ignoring a nonpositive denominator.

cards.prompt: Define BFGS curvature condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The positivity y_k transpose s_k>0 that preserves positive definiteness under a standard BFGS update from a PD approximation.
required_concepts: The positivity y_k transpose s_k>0 that preserves positive definiteness under a standard BFGS update from a PD approximation.
major_error_concepts: Treating nonzero y transpose s as sufficient regardless of sign.

cards.prompt: Define BFGS inverse update. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The formula H_next=(I-rho s y transpose)H(I-rho y s transpose)+rho s s transpose with rho=1/(y transpose s) under the positive-curvature condition.
required_concepts: The formula H_next=(I-rho s y transpose)H(I-rho y s transpose)+rho s s transpose with rho=1/(y transpose s) under the positive-curvature condition.
major_error_concepts: Substituting the DFP inverse formula or the direct-Hessian BFGS formula while labeling it the BFGS inverse update.

cards.prompt: Define Damped Newton method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A Newton direction combined with a line search or step fraction to globalize progress beyond the local full-step regime.
required_concepts: A Newton direction combined with a line search or step fraction to globalize progress beyond the local full-step regime.
major_error_concepts: Accepting alpha=1 because Newton is locally fast.

cards.prompt: Define Gradient finite-difference check. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The comparison of an analytic directional or coordinate gradient with a carefully stepped finite-difference approximation.
required_concepts: The comparison of an analytic directional or coordinate gradient with a carefully stepped finite-difference approximation.
major_error_concepts: Using one extremely tiny h and treating cancellation error as proof the analytic gradient is wrong.

cards.prompt: Define Hessian-vector product. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The product H(x)v computed directly or by directional differentiation without materializing the complete Hessian.
required_concepts: The product H(x)v computed directly or by directional differentiation without materializing the complete Hessian.
major_error_concepts: Confusing H v with the scalar v transpose H v.

cards.prompt: Define Indefinite-Hessian Newton failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The case where the Newton direction is not descent because the local quadratic has negative curvature.
required_concepts: The case where the Newton direction is not descent because the local quadratic has negative curvature.
major_error_concepts: Assuming an invertible Hessian guarantees a descent direction.

cards.prompt: Define Local quadratic convergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The asymptotic error relation norm(e_{k+1})<=C norm(e_k)^2 near a nondegenerate solution under smooth Hessian assumptions and full accepted steps.
required_concepts: The asymptotic error relation norm(e_{k+1})<=C norm(e_k)^2 near a nondegenerate solution under smooth Hessian assumptions and full accepted steps.
major_error_concepts: Calling a parabolic-looking loss plot proof of quadratic convergence from any initialization.

cards.prompt: Define Modified Hessian. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A positive-definite adjustment such as H+lambda I used to obtain a solvable descent-producing local model.
required_concepts: A positive-definite adjustment such as H+lambda I used to obtain a solvable descent-producing local model.
major_error_concepts: Using lambda=2 and calling the shifted Hessian positive definite when it may be singular.

cards.prompt: Define Newton equation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The linear system H_k p_k=-g_k whose solution minimizes the quadratic model when H_k is positive definite.
required_concepts: The linear system H_k p_k=-g_k whose solution minimizes the quadratic model when H_k is positive definite.
major_error_concepts: Computing p=-H g instead of solving H p=-g.

cards.prompt: Define Newton optimization iteration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The update x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k or a damped version using a Hessian-based direction.
required_concepts: The update x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k or a damped version using a Hessian-based direction.
major_error_concepts: Calling any Hessian-scaled gradient update full Newton without the Newton equation.

cards.prompt: Define Newton step for a quadratic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact solution correction -Q inverse(Qx+q) for an SPD unconstrained quadratic, reaching the optimizer in one exact full step.
required_concepts: The exact solution correction -Q inverse(Qx+q) for an SPD unconstrained quadratic, reaching the optimizer in one exact full step.
major_error_concepts: Claiming one-step convergence for a general nonquadratic objective.

cards.prompt: Define Quasi-Newton method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An iteration replacing the exact Hessian or its inverse with an updated approximation built from gradient differences.
required_concepts: An iteration replacing the exact Hessian or its inverse with an updated approximation built from gradient differences.
major_error_concepts: Calling finite-difference Hessian computation itself a quasi-Newton update.

cards.prompt: Define Secant condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement B_{k+1}s_k=y_k or H_{k+1}y_k=s_k under the declared Hessian or inverse-Hessian convention.
required_concepts: The requirement B_{k+1}s_k=y_k or H_{k+1}y_k=s_k under the declared Hessian or inverse-Hessian convention.
major_error_concepts: Mixing Hessian and inverse-Hessian formulas.

cards.prompt: Define Secant pair. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The displacement s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k and gradient change y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k used in quasi-Newton updates.
required_concepts: The displacement s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k and gradient change y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k used in quasi-Newton updates.
major_error_concepts: Swapping y with the objective-value difference.

cards.prompt: Define Optimization quadratic local model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The local quadratic m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k transpose p+one-half p transpose H_k p used to propose rather than automatically certify a step.
required_concepts: The local quadratic m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k transpose p+one-half p transpose H_k p used to propose rather than automatically certify a step.
major_error_concepts: Calling the truncated model exact away from the expansion point.

cards.prompt: Define Singular-Hessian Newton failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The case where H p=-g has no unique stable solution and the local model may be flat or underdetermined.
required_concepts: The case where H p=-g has no unique stable solution and the local model may be flat or underdetermined.
major_error_concepts: Dividing by a nearly zero Hessian without a safeguard.

cards.prompt: Define Trust-region acceptance and radius update. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified rule linking rho to step acceptance and contraction or expansion of Delta.
required_concepts: The specified rule linking rho to step acceptance and contraction or expansion of Delta.
major_error_concepts: Expanding the radius after poor model agreement.

cards.prompt: Define Trust region model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The constrained local subproblem minimizing a model over norm(p)<=Delta where model reliability controls the radius.
required_concepts: The constrained local subproblem minimizing a model over norm(p)<=Delta where model reliability controls the radius.
major_error_concepts: Calling the trust-region constraint an original model constraint.

cards.prompt: Define Active-set interpretation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The subset of inequalities binding at a candidate and locally behaving like equalities subject to regularity and correct multiplier signs.
required_concepts: The subset of inequalities binding at a candidate and locally behaving like equalities subject to regularity and correct multiplier signs.
major_error_concepts: Freezing an active set from one iterate as globally permanent.

cards.prompt: Define Complementary slackness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The products lambda_i g_i(x)=0 linking positive multipliers only to active constraints at a KKT point.
required_concepts: The products lambda_i g_i(x)=0 linking positive multipliers only to active constraints at a KKT point.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every active constraint has a positive multiplier.

cards.prompt: Define Constraint qualification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A regularity condition such as LICQ or Slater that enables specified KKT necessity or strong-duality conclusions rather than an optimization objective itself.
required_concepts: A regularity condition such as LICQ or Slater that enables specified KKT necessity or strong-duality conclusions rather than an optimization objective itself.
major_error_concepts: Calling differentiability alone a constraint qualification.

cards.prompt: Define Equality-constrained problem. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A model minimizing f(x) subject to h(x)=0 with feasibility and tangent directions determined by the equality map.
required_concepts: A model minimizing f(x) subject to h(x)=0 with feasibility and tangent directions determined by the equality map.
major_error_concepts: Solving the unconstrained gradient equation and ignoring the equality.

cards.prompt: Define Equality KKT system. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The stationarity gradient f+J_h transpose nu=0 and primal feasibility h=0 for a regular equality-constrained candidate.
required_concepts: The stationarity gradient f+J_h transpose nu=0 and primal feasibility h=0 for a regular equality-constrained candidate.
major_error_concepts: Solving stationarity but omitting feasibility.

cards.prompt: Define Equality Lagrangian. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The scalar L(x,nu)=f(x)+nu transpose h(x) under a frozen equality sign convention.
required_concepts: The scalar L(x,nu)=f(x)+nu transpose h(x) under a frozen equality sign convention.
major_error_concepts: Changing h to 1-x-y without changing multiplier interpretations.

cards.prompt: Define Equality rank condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The linear independence or full-row-rank property supporting multiplier and KKT-system regularity, distinct from feasibility.
required_concepts: The linear independence or full-row-rank property supporting multiplier and KKT-system regularity, distinct from feasibility.
major_error_concepts: Calling redundancy proof the primal problem is infeasible.

cards.prompt: Define Euclidean projection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The nearest-point map Pi_C(z)=argmin_{x in C} one-half ||x-z||^2 for a nonempty closed convex set C.
required_concepts: C is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Pi_C(z)=argmin_{x in C} one-half ||x-z||^2.
major_error_concepts: Clipping to the wrong interval endpoint.

cards.prompt: Distinguish a straight-line feasible direction from tangent or linearized feasibility, using a curved-constraint example.
cards.definition: At x in a feasible set C, a straight-line feasible direction d has some epsilon>0 such that x+t d belongs to C for all 0≤t≤epsilon. Tangent directions describe first-order limits of feasible displacements and need not generate feasible straight rays. For differentiable constraints, linearized conditions such as J_h(x)d=0 and grad g_i(x)^T d≤0 for active inequalities are necessary first-order tests, not sufficient in general for straight-line feasibility. At (1,0) on the unit circle, (0,1) is tangent but its positive straight steps leave the circle.
required_concepts: Straight-line feasibility requires an actual small ray segment inside C.
Tangent or linearized feasibility alone can be weaker.
Curved constraints can make a tangent straight step infeasible.
major_error_concepts: Every vector satisfying J_h(x)d=0 gives x+t d feasible for sufficiently small positive t, even for a curved equality constraint.

cards.prompt: What does Inequality constraint convention denote, including its domain or type when relevant?
cards.definition: **Definition.** The frozen representation g_i(x)<=0 with multiplier lambda_i>=0 used throughout KKT and dual derivations.
required_concepts: The frozen representation g_i(x)<=0 with multiplier lambda_i>=0 used throughout KKT and dual derivations.
major_error_concepts: For an intended constraint x>=1, writing g(x)=x-1<=0 encodes x<=1 and reverses the feasible set.

cards.prompt: What does Inequality Lagrangian denote, including its domain or type when relevant?
cards.definition: **Definition.** The function L(x,lambda,nu)=f(x)+sum lambda_i g_i(x)+nu transpose h(x) with lambda>=0 for g<=0.
required_concepts: The function L(x,lambda,nu)=f(x)+sum lambda_i g_i(x)+nu transpose h(x) with lambda>=0 for g<=0.
major_error_concepts: Using a negative multiplier while retaining the g<=0 convention.

cards.prompt: Define KKT dual feasibility. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The sign requirement lambda_i>=0 associated with minimized problems and g_i<=0.
required_concepts: The sign requirement lambda_i>=0 associated with minimized problems and g_i<=0.
major_error_concepts: Changing multiplier sign to make stationarity work.

cards.prompt: What is KKT necessity and sufficiency used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It separates when KKT conditions must hold at a local optimum from when satisfying KKT certifies global optimality; the two directions use different regularity and convexity assumptions.
required_concepts: Constraint qualification governs the necessity direction.
Convexity and affine equalities govern the sufficiency direction.
major_error_concepts: Treating KKT as a universal necessary-and-sufficient test without checking either direction's assumptions.

cards.prompt: For minimizing f(x) subject to g_i(x)<=0 and h_j(x)=0, state the KKT necessity result under LICQ and the separate convex sufficiency result, including each direction's hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** Consider minimizing differentiable f(x) subject to differentiable g_i(x)<=0 and h_j(x)=0. Necessity: if x* is a local minimizer and LICQ holds there, meaning the active inequality gradients together with the equality gradients are linearly independent, then KKT multipliers exist at x*. Sufficiency: if f is convex and differentiable, every g_i is convex and differentiable, and every h_j is affine, then any point and multipliers satisfying primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementary slackness give a global minimizer.
required_concepts: Necessity assumes differentiable f, g_i, and h_j and a local minimizer x*.
LICQ means the active inequality gradients and equality gradients are linearly independent at x*.
Under those necessity hypotheses, KKT multipliers exist at x*.
Sufficiency assumes convex differentiable f, convex differentiable g_i, and affine h_j.
The candidate and multipliers satisfy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementary slackness.
Under those sufficiency hypotheses and KKT conditions, the candidate is a global minimizer.
major_error_concepts: Using KKT as a universal solver and certificate.

cards.prompt: Define KKT primal feasibility. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement g_i(x)<=0 and h(x)=0 at a KKT candidate.
required_concepts: The requirement g_i(x)<=0 and h(x)=0 at a KKT candidate.
major_error_concepts: Treating stationarity as enough.

cards.prompt: Define KKT saddle-point matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The block linear system [[H,A transpose],[A,0]] for equality-constrained quadratic steps or solutions.
required_concepts: The block linear system [[H,A transpose],[A,0]] for equality-constrained quadratic steps or solutions.
major_error_concepts: Putting a positive identity matrix in the multiplier block without changing the problem.

cards.prompt: Define KKT stationarity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The vanishing x-gradient of the Lagrangian at the candidate under differentiability.
required_concepts: The vanishing x-gradient of the Lagrangian at the candidate under differentiability.
major_error_concepts: Using gradient f=0 despite an active constraint.

cards.prompt: Define Projected gradient method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The iteration x_{k+1}=Pi_C(x_k-alpha gradient f(x_k)) for a projection-friendly convex constraint set.
required_concepts: The iteration x_{k+1}=Pi_C(x_k-alpha gradient f(x_k)) for a projection-friendly convex constraint set.
major_error_concepts: Projecting the gradient rather than the trial point without defining a tangent method.

cards.prompt: Define Projected-gradient residual. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A scaled difference G_alpha(x)=(x-Pi_C(x-alpha gradient f(x)))/alpha that generalizes stationarity for convex constraints.
required_concepts: A scaled difference G_alpha(x)=(x-Pi_C(x-alpha gradient f(x)))/alpha that generalizes stationarity for convex constraints.
major_error_concepts: Rejecting a boundary optimum because its raw gradient is nonzero.

cards.prompt: Define Projection optimality condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The variational inequality (z-xproj) transpose(y-xproj)<=0 for every y in C under the Euclidean projection convention.
required_concepts: The variational inequality (z-xproj) transpose(y-xproj)<=0 for every y in C under the Euclidean projection convention.
major_error_concepts: Using equality instead of inequality for a general convex set.

cards.prompt: State the reduced-Hessian necessary and sufficient curvature conditions for a regular equality-constrained KKT point.
cards.definition: For a C² equality-constrained problem, suppose x* is feasible, equality gradients are independent, and KKT stationarity holds with multiplier nu*. Let Z span ker J_h(x*) and H=Hessian_x L(x*,nu*). A necessary second-order condition for a local minimum is Z^T H Z positive semidefinite; positive definiteness on every nonzero tangent direction is sufficient for a strict local minimum under these assumptions. Ambient positive definiteness is stronger than necessary but is a valid sufficient way to establish positive tangent curvature.
required_concepts: Use the Lagrangian Hessian and the feasible tangent space under equality regularity.
Restricted positive semidefiniteness is necessary; restricted positive definiteness is sufficient with KKT and regularity.
A stronger valid ambient positive-definiteness check must not be penalized.
major_error_concepts: A positive-semidefinite reduced Hessian by itself, without feasibility or stationarity, certifies a strict constrained minimum.

cards.prompt: Define Complementarity from gap decomposition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The link between zero gap and terms lambda_i[-f_i(x)] whose nonnegative sum must vanish under compatible optimality conditions.
required_concepts: The link between zero gap and terms lambda_i[-f_i(x)] whose nonnegative sum must vanish under compatible optimality conditions.
major_error_concepts: Treating complementarity as an independent causal law.

cards.prompt: Define Dual attainment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The existence of multipliers achieving d star, which is separate from equality of primal and dual optimal values.
required_concepts: The existence of multipliers achieving d star, which is separate from equality of primal and dual optimal values.
major_error_concepts: Treating a supremum as automatically attained.

cards.prompt: Define Dual certificate verification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The independent recomputation of multiplier signs stationarity feasibility complementarity objective values and gap before accepting a dual claim.
required_concepts: The independent recomputation of multiplier signs stationarity feasibility complementarity objective values and gap before accepting a dual claim.
major_error_concepts: Trusting solver dual fields without checking the constraint convention.

cards.term: Scope of dual decomposition in Optimization I
cards.prompt: Define Scope of dual decomposition in Optimization I. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The observation that separable minimization of a Lagrangian can expose structure, while full decomposition algorithms belong downstream.
required_concepts: The observation that separable minimization of a Lagrangian can expose structure, while full decomposition algorithms belong downstream.
major_error_concepts: Presenting ADMM or distributed convergence as covered here.

cards.prompt: Define Dual feasible set. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The multipliers satisfying sign and domain requirements for which the dual function is used as a valid lower bound.
required_concepts: The multipliers satisfying sign and domain requirements for which the dual function is used as a valid lower bound.
major_error_concepts: Constraining equality multipliers to be nonnegative.

cards.prompt: Define Dual variable as shadow price. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The qualified local marginal value associated with a right-hand-side perturbation under a frozen sign convention and regular value function.
required_concepts: The qualified local marginal value associated with a right-hand-side perturbation under a frozen sign convention and regular value function.
major_error_concepts: Calling it a global price valid for arbitrary perturbations.

cards.prompt: Define Lagrange dual function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The infimum over primal variables g(lambda,nu)=inf_x L(x,lambda,nu), which is concave in dual variables even when the primal is not convex.
required_concepts: The infimum over primal variables g(lambda,nu)=inf_x L(x,lambda,nu), which is concave in dual variables even when the primal is not convex.
major_error_concepts: Evaluating L at an arbitrary x and calling it the dual function.

cards.prompt: Define Lagrange dual problem. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The maximization of the concave dual function over dual-feasible multipliers.
required_concepts: The maximization of the concave dual function over dual-feasible multipliers.
major_error_concepts: Minimizing the dual function because the primal was a minimization.

cards.prompt: Define Local sensitivity qualification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The active-set stability differentiability uniqueness or envelope conditions restricting a multiplier-based derivative claim.
required_concepts: The active-set stability differentiability uniqueness or envelope conditions restricting a multiplier-based derivative claim.
major_error_concepts: Using a shadow price far outside the local regime.

cards.prompt: Define LP and nonlinear duality distinction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The boundary between LP dual construction and general Lagrangian dual derivation, which can agree after conventions but are not copied mechanically.
required_concepts: The boundary between LP dual construction and general Lagrangian dual derivation, which can agree after conventions but are not copied mechanically.
major_error_concepts: Applying an LP transpose template to a nonlinear constraint.

cards.prompt: Define Perturbation value function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The optimal objective p(u,v) of a family with perturbed inequality and equality right sides.
required_concepts: The optimal objective p(u,v) of a family with perturbed inequality and equality right sides.
major_error_concepts: Differentiating f(x) while ignoring that the optimizer changes.

cards.prompt: Define Primal-dual gap. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The nonnegative difference f0(x)-g(lambda,nu) for a primal-feasible point and dual-feasible multipliers.
required_concepts: The nonnegative difference f0(x)-g(lambda,nu) for a primal-feasible point and dual-feasible multipliers.
major_error_concepts: Computing a gap from an infeasible primal point without a qualified bound.

cards.prompt: Define Primal problem convention. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The fixed minimization problem p star=inf f0(x) subject to f_i(x)<=0 and h_j(x)=0 from which one dual is derived.
required_concepts: The fixed minimization problem p star=inf f0(x) subject to f_i(x)<=0 and h_j(x)=0 from which one dual is derived.
major_error_concepts: Switching to maximization halfway through the derivation.

cards.prompt: Define Sensitivity sign convention. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit mapping from a perturbation parameter to the Lagrangian ensuring the multiplier derivative sign is not guessed.
required_concepts: The explicit mapping from a perturbation parameter to the Lagrangian ensuring the multiplier derivative sign is not guessed.
major_error_concepts: Reporting +lambda without checking how u enters.

cards.prompt: Define Slater condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** For a convex problem, Slater condition is the existence of a point in the relative interior of the common domain that strictly satisfies every inequality constraint and satisfies every affine equality; it is a sufficient qualification for the standard strong-duality and KKT conclusions.
required_concepts: A Slater point lies in the relative interior of the common domain, strictly satisfies every inequality constraint, and satisfies every affine equality.
For a convex problem, that condition is a sufficient qualification for the standard strong-duality and KKT conclusions.
major_error_concepts: Using the boundary point x=1 as strict feasibility.

cards.prompt: Define Strong duality. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The equality d star=p star under a theorem's specified conditions, distinct from weak duality and attainment.
required_concepts: The equality d star=p star under a theorem's specified conditions, distinct from weak duality and attainment.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every convex problem has strong duality without a qualification.

cards.prompt: Define Weak duality. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The inequality g(lambda,nu)<=p star for every dual-feasible multiplier in the minimization convention.
required_concepts: The inequality g(lambda,nu)<=p star for every dual-feasible multiplier in the minimization convention.
major_error_concepts: Calling a lower bound an achievable primal objective.

cards.prompt: Define Zero-gap optimality certificate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The conclusion that primal and dual feasible objects with equal objectives are both optimal.
required_concepts: The conclusion that primal and dual feasible objects with equal objectives are both optimal.
major_error_concepts: Claiming uniqueness from zero gap.

cards.prompt: Define algorithm initialization.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The starting point and feasibility status supplied to an iterative method, including whether the method requires or restores feasibility.
required_concepts: The starting point and feasibility status supplied to an iterative method, including whether the method requires or restores feasibility.
major_error_concepts: Omitting x0 because the final objective looked good.

cards.prompt: Define Complementarity residual. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The magnitude of multiplier-slack products with sign and feasibility checks retained separately.
required_concepts: The magnitude of multiplier-slack products with sign and feasibility checks retained separately.
major_error_concepts: Using a small product to excuse a negative multiplier.

cards.prompt: Define Constraint reconstruction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The independent evaluation of every original-domain bound equality and inequality rather than only transformed internal constraints.
required_concepts: The independent evaluation of every original-domain bound equality and inequality rather than only transformed internal constraints.
major_error_concepts: Checking only the solver's scaled residual summary.

cards.prompt: Define DCP curvature analysis.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The recursive sign and curvature analysis used to certify that a CVXPY expression follows disciplined convex programming rules.
required_concepts: The recursive sign and curvature analysis used to certify that a CVXPY expression follows disciplined convex programming rules.
major_error_concepts: Calling DCP rejection proof the mathematical function is nonconvex.

cards.prompt: Define Duality-gap residual. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The absolute or signed primal-minus-dual objective difference computed only for feasible compatible primal-dual objects.
required_concepts: The absolute or signed primal-minus-dual objective difference computed only for feasible compatible primal-dual objects.
major_error_concepts: Taking absolute difference of incompatible objective conventions.

cards.prompt: Define Linear-solve residual. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The norm of A x-b or H p+g used to verify a numerical linear system underlying an optimization step.
required_concepts: The norm of A x-b or H p+g used to verify a numerical linear system underlying an optimization step.
major_error_concepts: Checking only that a linear solver returned without error.

cards.prompt: Define Objective reconstruction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The independent recomputation of the objective and each component from the returned variables and frozen data.
required_concepts: The independent recomputation of the objective and each component from the returned variables and frozen data.
major_error_concepts: Copying solver.fun into the report without evaluation.

cards.prompt: Define Optimization guarantee versus learning guarantee. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The boundary where this course supplies objectives gradients curvature constraints convergence and certificates while ML decks own empirical risk generalization minibatches adaptive optimizers and deep training behavior.
required_concepts: This course supplies objectives, gradients, curvature, constraints, convergence results, and certificates.
Machine-learning courses own empirical-risk, generalization, minibatch, adaptive-optimizer, and deep-training claims.
major_error_concepts: Using a convex theorem to guarantee a nonconvex stochastic training run.

cards.prompt: Define Perturbation and multistart diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A controlled rerun over declared initial points, tolerances, or scaling choices used to reveal solver-result sensitivity or numerical fragility; agreement across reruns still does not prove global optimality.
required_concepts: The diagnostic reruns the same declared problem across initial points, tolerances, or scaling choices and compares the resulting candidates and residuals.
Disagreement diagnoses solver-result sensitivity or numerical fragility, while agreement still does not prove global optimality.
major_error_concepts: Calling the best of ten starts the global optimum.

cards.prompt: Define Primal feasibility residual. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The maximum or normed violation of bounds equalities and inequalities under a declared scaling.
required_concepts: The maximum or normed violation of bounds equalities and inequalities under a declared scaling.
major_error_concepts: Taking absolute values of inactive negative inequalities and calling them violations.

cards.prompt: Define Qualified optimization result. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A qualified optimization result reports the declared model and assumptions, candidate point, solver status, objective and constraint residuals, stationarity evidence, tolerances, and the exact scope of any certificate without extending the conclusion beyond those assumptions and checks.
required_concepts: The result reports the declared model and assumptions, candidate point, solver status, objective and constraint residuals, stationarity evidence, and tolerances.
Any optimality conclusion is limited to the exact scope of an applicable certificate and its checked assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Declaring a global optimum from a success flag when no applicable global certificate and assumption check has been supplied.

cards.prompt: Define Solver compatibility. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The match among problem class cone or derivative requirements constraints bounds and installed numerical backend.
required_concepts: The match among problem class cone or derivative requirements constraints bounds and installed numerical backend.
major_error_concepts: Treating installation as support for all models.

cards.prompt: Define Solver termination status. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The implementation-reported reason a run stopped, which is evidence to investigate rather than a mathematical certificate by itself.
required_concepts: The implementation-reported reason a run stopped, which is evidence to investigate rather than a mathematical certificate by itself.
major_error_concepts: Equating success true with global optimality.

cards.prompt: Define Stationarity residual. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The norm of the objective gradient for unconstrained problems or the Lagrangian/projected residual appropriate to constraints.
required_concepts: The norm of the objective gradient for unconstrained problems or the Lagrangian/projected residual appropriate to constraints.
major_error_concepts: Rejecting the point because raw gradient is nonzero.

cards.prompt: Define stopping tolerances.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The separate numerical thresholds for optimality feasibility step objective barrier trust region and iteration termination under solver-specific meanings.
required_concepts: The separate numerical thresholds for optimality feasibility step objective barrier trust region and iteration termination under solver-specific meanings.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every solver's tol field has the same mathematical meaning.

description: A definition-recall course deck covering core concepts in Optimization I.
